description: Issue #867 (PR #884 cross-vendor review point 6): neutralizes RequestBindingPolicy.Classify's ambiguous-resolution guard (`if (members.Length > 1) { ... return BindingRejectionReason.AmbiguousMember; }`, src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Helper/RequestBindingPolicy.cs) with a compile-preserving `&& false` (not a deletion). Issue #1080 moved this guard's walk out of IsPathAllowed and into Classify, which now returns a BindingRejectionReason instead of bool; IsPathAllowed(Type, string, string) is a pure delegation (`Classify(...) == BindingRejectionReason.None`), so this mutant still turns IsPathAllowed's own assertion red -- see the 'With the guard neutralized' sentence below. PropertyHelper.SetPropertyValue's own traversal unconditionally takes GetMember(...)[0]; the review's point was that this policy must not implicitly trust that ordering to be the safe candidate when Type.GetMember returns more than one member for a name. Empirically verified which C# shape actually produces that (not assumed): same-kind hiding (a property hidden by a `new` property of the same name, as in RequestBindingPolicyTests867's ShadowVM) does NOT -- .NET's reflection resolves that down to the single most-derived member before this policy ever sees it -- but hiding ACROSS member kinds (a base class FIELD hidden by a derived class PROPERTY of the same name) does: `typeof(AmbiguousShadowVM).GetMember("Label").Length == 2`, confirmed by a sanity assertion inside the test itself. Checked against RequestBindingPolicyTests867.IsPathAllowed_FieldHiddenByPropertyOfSameName_ReturnsFalse, where neither candidate member individually resolves to a banned gateway type (both are plain strings) -- isolating this guard from the gateway-type guard. With the guard neutralized, Classify reaches the `var member = members[0];` line and evaluates only that one candidate, returning BindingRejectionReason.None instead of AmbiguousMember; because IsPathAllowed is a pure delegation to Classify, IsPathAllowed(vm, "Label") also returns true instead of false, which is what turns the assertion red. The green control, IsPathAllowed_SearcherDotCustomFilterField_ReturnsTrue, exercises an unambiguous legitimate path and is genuinely unaffected by this mutant.
target_symbol: RequestBindingPolicy.Classify(Type, string, string) -- the `if (members.Length > 1) { ... return BindingRejectionReason.AmbiguousMember; }` ambiguous-resolution guard condition (IsPathAllowed(Type, string, string) is now a pure delegation to Classify, per Issue #1080)

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Helper.Request: this policy must fail closed on ambiguity rather than trust members\[0\]

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Re-captured verbatim (issue #1080 refactor: patch retargeted from IsPathAllowed to Classify) against a clean checkout with the regenerated mutant patch applied (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first): 'Assert.IsFalse failed. #867/PR#884 review point 6: Type.GetMember can return more than one member for the same name (a field hidden by a differently-kinded property is the verified concrete case) — this policy must fail closed on ambiguity rather than trust members[0] to be the safe one, even when neither candidate individually resolves to a banned gateway type.'. Confirmed via python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant wtmsec867-ambiguous-resolution-guard-neutralize: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
